title: Music and dance steps: one step, two step, three step, quadrille
summary: Arthur compares old ragtime dance music with today's and describes one-step, two-step, three-step and the quadrille dance with 'Three Little Blackberries'.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Well, I don't know. It's almost about like the Dixieland music is, but the regular, what I'd say called ragtime music. Well, there's a big change in ragtime music from the days of my daddy when they played like for a dance. There's a big difference in the music of today and in their times. The music they played in them times was mostly a one step, a two step, or a three step dance. But you couldn't dance in all the music they're playing today.

Can you tell us, we've never talked to many people about the dancing since you didn't go into music. I mean, could you tell us anything about the dancing, the difference between the one step, two step, and three? I know it may be hard to describe in words.
Well, it all depends on the time of the music for those different dances.

Well, a three step would be the fastest. Three step. Yeah, then a two step, and then a one step would be a slow piece. Then in them times you've danced more waltzes than you do now, and shardesses then. They played a lot of shardesses in them times. I had just learned how to shardesses real well when they went out. And the lady would have thought that she died about two years ago. She died at the age of 80 some odd. But I was nothing but a kid, but she was a wonderful shardess dancer. And during the time when my brother was playing, when they used to play for a shardess, I don't know if you remember that piece. They used to play a piece, three little blackberries. You ever heard of that number? No, I don't remember that. That's the number they used to play for a shardess, three little blackberries. I think if I had fat around you I could make it play it for you. Fat could play it for you. Probably.

But I remember those dances and them times are so different from now. And at the age I am now I love to dance. I love to dance. My wife and I go out dancing twice a week. I take all them late dances like Cha Cha and Chitterbug and all that kind of stuff. I go away with that at the age I am now. But I did like dancing better than I liked the music. I always did dance.
